candidate.educational_objective: Use Standard plus Droplet Precautions for routine care of a hospitalized client with seasonal influenza.

options.A: Use Standard plus Droplet Precautions, including a mask for healthcare personnel during close care and source control for transport.
options.B: Use Standard plus Airborne Precautions with an N95 respirator for all routine care until every respiratory symptom has resolved.
options.C: Use Standard plus Contact Precautions with gown and gloves for all room entry because influenza spreads mainly through surfaces.
options.D: Use Standard Precautions alone once antiviral therapy begins because treatment promptly removes the need for transmission-based precautions.

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance for seasonal influenza in healthcare settings requires Standard Precautions plus Droplet Precautions for suspected or confirmed influenza. Airborne infection isolation is not routinely required for ordinary influenza care, although respiratory protection may be indicated for aerosol-generating procedures under facility guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Routine care for suspected or confirmed seasonal influenza uses Standard plus Droplet Precautions; routine airborne isolation is not required outside aerosol-risk circumstances.
